8) Locate relevant columns (status, customer, date, grand total) by checking header substrings. Build list-of-dicts for rows.

9) Filter rows with status containing 'cancel' (case-insensitive). If none, print 0.00 and return.

10) Count cancellations per customer (use customer name or email if available). Select the customer with the most cancellations; break ties by lexicographic order.

11) For that customer, collect their cancelled orders. Parse dates (several common formats). Determine the most recent timestamp among parsed dates; if some parsed, take all orders whose parsed date equals the most recent (to handle multiple orders at identical most-recent timestamp). If no dates parsed, fall back to the last row as the most recent.

13) Print the sum formatted with two decimals, and nothing else.
